result:
The final pick is an adaptive LIRS policy in `final.py`. It scores **0.574** on the official search split, against 0.365 for the LRU baseline. I used **5 of the 24 scorer calls**.

| | Search (official) | Held-out (my harness, seeds 1000–1007) |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (LRU) | 0.365 | 0.424 |
| First champion (W-TinyLFU) | 0.503 | 0.445 |
| LIRS | 0.567 | 0.491 |
| **Final (adaptive LIRS)** | **0.574** | **0.501** |

**Why it beats LRU:**
- **Loops and scans:** LIRS keeps keys that are reused at short intervals in a protected block that holds most of the cache. Keys seen once go to a small separate area and leave quickly. A loop longer than the cache therefore keeps part of itself cached instead of missing every time as it does under LRU. On the official `shifting_loops` trace this gives 0.82, against 0.16 for ARC.
- **History length:** LIRS remembers keys it has already evicted, up to 8× the capacity. On my harness this mattered more than any other setting (0.390 → 0.413).
- **Recency:** I added an ARC-style adjustment. When a miss is on a key that was evicted recently from the small area, that area grows; when it's on a key evicted from the protected block, it shrinks. This raised the `recency` trace from 0.77 to 0.85 (ARC's level) and cost a little on loops.
- **Capacity 1:** a guard sets the small area to zero, which avoids an overflow I found there.

**Approaches tried before LIRS (harness score / official score):**

| Approach | Harness | Official | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| ARC | 0.279 | 0.407 | best on recency, weak on loops |
| W-TinyLFU | 0.284 | 0.503 | strong on loops, weak on recency |
| S3-FIFO | 0.279 | not scored | about the same as ARC |
| TinyLFU with a self-tuning window | 0.316 | not scored | noisy, no better than TinyLFU |
| LIRS | 0.390 | 0.567 | best on both |

**Later rounds:** 11 more variants, none of them clearly better:
- Different adjustment speeds, minimum sizes, history sizes and starting sizes made no real difference.
- Using access counts to decide which keys enter the protected block gained about 0.01 on mixed traffic but lost up to 0.11 on loops.

After two rounds without improvement I stopped, which is the skill's stopping rule, and left 19 scorer calls unused.

**Edge cases:** I ran the final pick on unusual inputs: an empty trace, capacities 1–10, a single repeated key, huge and negative keys, fewer keys than the cache holds, all-unique keys, and a loop 20× the cache size. Only capacity 1 failed, and the guard fixes it without changing any score. All my local traces together run in about 0.4 s, well under the 8 s limit.

The two traces mixing hot keys with scans stay low, about 0.24–0.27, and no approach I tried did meaningfully better on them.

My harness first ranked TinyLFU below LRU because it had no recency-heavy traffic. After I added that, it ranked the strategies in the same order as the scorer. One early parameter sweep was invalid because Python reused stale compiled files, so I reran it with that caching turned off.

Everything is in the `cache/` folder; `log.md` has one line per candidate.
